field.label: Enable Tracking
field.comment: Kill switch — disables the frontend beacon and the ingest endpoint's writes entirely.

field.label: Primary Attribution Model
field.comment: docs/SPECS.md §4 — used to pick which touch populates ads_analytics_order_attribution.

field.label: Report Aggregation Lookback (days)
field.comment: How many recent days the nightly rollup recomputes. Events arrive through a queue, so a visit at 23:59 can be consumed after the 02:00 run — re-sweeping recent days picks those up. The rollup REPLACES each day it recomputes rather than adding to it, so a wider window costs time but can never double-count.

field.label: Beacon Console Logging
field.comment:
Makes the storefront beacon narrate every decision to the browser console: which event type it chose and why, consent and cookie state, each checkout step it detects, and whether each request was sent, deduplicated or suppressed. Leave this off in production — it is a diagnostic, not a feature.
You can also switch it on for one browsing session, without touching this setting, by adding ?adsanalytics_debug=1 to any storefront URL. That survives navigation, so it stays on through a whole landing → cart → checkout walkthrough. Turn it back off with ?adsanalytics_debug=0.

field.label: Sampling Rate (%)
field.comment: Optional load-shedding lever for high-traffic stores. Default 100.

group.label: Traffic Classification (Platforms & Search Engines)
group.comment: docs/SPECS.md §2. These three lists are the ONLY place a platform, paid medium or search engine is named. Adding Pinterest, or a new regional search engine, is a row here and no code change anywhere (CLAUDE.md #2). Defaults ship in etc/config.xml, so the store works out of the box and a later module version can add a platform without an admin having to notice.

field.label: Paid Platform / Click-ID Map
field.comment:
Click ID Parameter is the signal that classifies a visit as paid, and it is client-supplied — the queue consumer rejects any value not listed here (docs/SECURITY.md §2).
Default Source is what source becomes for this platform (meta → facebook).
Alt Sources are utm_source values that override Default Source when present — meta ships instagram, which is how an Instagram click is told apart from a Facebook one without naming either in code. platform_code itself never changes: it stays meta in both cases.

field.label: Paid Mediums (no click ID)
field.comment: For manually-tagged paid links that carry no click ID, e.g. ?utm_medium=cpc. Matched case-insensitively, so listing cpc also covers CPC.

field.label: Organic Search-Engine Domains
field.comment: Registrable domains only — google.com, never .google.com or google.*. Matched at a label boundary, so notgoogle.com does not match but mail.google.com does. Wildcards are unsupported by design: list each TLD as its own row mapping to the same engine name (yandex.com and yandex.ru → yandex).

field.label: How to provide spend data
field.comment:
ROAS (Model\Roas\RoasReportBuilder) needs a spend figure per platform, which the shipped provider reads from a CSV file — there is no field to type it into here.

File location: var/aavirbhava/adsanalytics/adspend/<platform_code>.csv (relative to the Magento install root), e.g. var/aavirbhava/adsanalytics/adspend/google.csv. Only platforms with a provider registered in etc/di.xml are read — by default that is google and meta, both sharing the same credential-free CSV reader. A platform with no file, or a platform with no provider at all, shows "no data" in the ROAS report rather than a zero.

Format: a header row, then one row per day/campaign: date,campaign,spend — date as YYYY-MM-DD, campaign matching the campaign name used in this store's UTM tagging, spend a plain decimal in the store's currency with no symbol (e.g. 2026-09-19,spring_sale,42.50). A malformed row is skipped and logged rather than rejecting the whole file.

This is a reference implementation, not a live feed from the ad platform — nothing updates this file automatically. A deployment with real Google Ads / Meta Ads API access can replace it with its own provider implementing Api\AdSpendProviderInterface, registered the same way, without touching this module's core (docs/SPECS.md §5).

group.label: Ingest Rate Limiting
group.comment:
docs/SECURITY.md §4. Enforced in Model\EventIngestService, at the webapi layer — deliberately NOT in the queue consumer, because by the time a consumer runs the request has already been accepted and queued, so a limit there sheds no load at all. Counters are cache-backed (never DB) and keyed on ip_hash + visitor_uuid together: the uuid alone is client-generated and rotatable, the ip alone is shared behind NAT.
Over the limit, events are dropped silently and the caller still gets a 200 — a tracking beacon must never surface its state to the storefront.

field.label: Max Requests Per Window
field.comment: Best-effort fixed window, not an exact quota — a concurrent burst can overshoot slightly. This is load shedding, not access control.

field.label: Logging Level
field.comment: docs/SPECS.md §9. Rejected + Externally Referred (default) logs invalid requests plus landings that arrived from a paid, organic or referral source — the ones whose URL can reveal a campaign parameter this module does not yet recognise. Direct arrivals and internal funnel events are not logged, because their URL carries no inbound source. Use All Requests temporarily when debugging the funnel itself; it stores raw payloads and full query strings for every request.

field.label: Request Log Retention (days)
field.comment: docs/SECURITY.md §8 — kept shorter than analytics-table retention below.

field.label: Raw Visit/Funnel Event Retention (days)
field.comment: Aggregated daily summary is retained indefinitely regardless of this setting.
